nodes.name: Wach module
nodes.statement: We write $\mathbb N(T)$ for the Wach module of $T$ (c.f. \cite{berger03,wach96}).

nodes.name: Fontaine/Berger isomorphism
nodes.statement: Then a result of Fontaine/Berger states that we have a canonical isomorphism $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)\cong \mathbb N(T)^{\psi=1}$ (we will identify these two objects throughout the paper).
nodes.statement_short: Iwasawa cohomology of T over Q_p is canonically isomorphic to the psi=1 part of the Wach module.
conclusions: we have a canonical isomorphism $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)\cong \mathbb N(T)^{\psi=1}$

nodes.name: Plus/minus Iwasawa cohomology over Q_p
nodes.statement:
Define
   \[ H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)^i=\left\{ x\in \mathbb N(T)^{\psi=1}\mid \varphi(x_i)=-p\psi(x_i)\right\},\]
  and let $H^1(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),T)^i$ be the image of $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)^i$ under the natural projection map $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)\rightarrow H^1(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Subgroup of N(T)^{psi=1} cut out by phi(x_i)=-p psi(x_i), and its images at finite level.

nodes.name: Signed local condition over Q_p(mu_{p^n})
nodes.statement: Define $H^1_{f,i}(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),E_{p^\infty})$ to be the exact annihilator of $H^1(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),T)^i$ under the Tate pairing.

nodes.name: Kobayashi plus/minus Selmer group
nodes.statement: One then defines $\mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash \mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))$ by replacing the usual local condition $H^1_{f}(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),E_{p^\infty})$ at the unique prime of $\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n})$ above $p$ by $H^1_{f,i}(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),E_{p^\infty})$.

nodes.name: Categories of p-adic representations
nodes.statement: Write $\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Z_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$ (resp. $\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Q_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$) for the category of finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-modules (resp. finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q_p$-vector spaces) with a continuous action of $\mathcal{G}_F$.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic tower of Q_p
nodes.statement: For an integer $n\geq 1$, we write $\mathbb Q_{p,n}=\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n})$, $\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}=\varinjlim \mathbb Q_{p,n}$ and $\Gamma=\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}\slash\mathbb Q_p)$.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic tower of F
nodes.statement: More generally, if $F$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, we write $F_n=F(\mu_{p^n})$, $F_\infty=\varinjlim F_n$, $H_F=\mathrm{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb Q_p}\slash F_\infty)$ and $\Gamma_F=\mathrm{Gal}(F_{\infty}\slash F)$.
also_stated_at: If $F$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, we write $F_n=F(\mu_{p^n})$.

nodes.name: Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: For $T\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Z_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$, define $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(F,T)=\varprojlim H^1(F_n,T)$ where the connecting maps are corestrictions $\mathrm{cor}_{n/m}:H^1(F_n,T)\rightarrow H^1(F_m,T)$ for $n\ge m$.

nodes.name: Rational Iwasawa cohomology
nodes.statement: If $V\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Q_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$, let $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(F,V)=H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(F,T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p$, where $T$ is a $\mathcal{G}_F$-invariant lattice of $V$.

nodes.name: Iwasawa algebra
nodes.statement: If $G$ is a compact $p$-adic Lie group, we write $\Lambda(G)=\mathbb Z_p[[G]]$ for its completed group ring over $\mathbb Z_p$.

nodes.name: Maximal extension unramified outside S
nodes.statement: For a finite set $S$ of primes of $\mathbb Q$, let $F_S$ denote the maximal algebraic extension of $\mathbb Q$ unramified outside $S$.

nodes.name: Galois group G_S(K)
nodes.statement: For an extension $K$ of $\mathbb Q$ contained in $F_S$, we write $G_S(K)=\mathrm{Gal}(F_S\slash K)$.

nodes.name: C_p
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathbb Q_p}$ be an algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q_p$, and write $\mathbb{C}_p$ for its $p$-adic completion.

nodes.name: Tilt ring E-tilde
nodes.statement:
Define
   \[ \tilde{\mathbb E}=\varprojlim_{x\rightarrow x^p} \mathbb{C}_p = \left\{ (x^{(0)},x^{(1)},\dots)\mid \left(x^{(i+1)}\right)^p=x^{(i)}\right\},\]
   and let $\tilde{\mathbb E}^+=\left\{x\in\tilde{\mathbb E}\mid x^{(0)}\in \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{C}_p}\right\}$.

nodes.name: E-tilde is an algebraically closed field
nodes.statement: Under these operations, $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$.
conclusions: $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$

nodes.name: Valuation on E-tilde
nodes.statement: Define a valuation on $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ by $v_{\tilde{\mathbb E}}(x)=v_p(x^{(0)})$.

nodes.name: epsilon and pi-bar
nodes.statement: Let $\varepsilon=(\varepsilon^{(i)})$ be a fixed element of $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ such that $\varepsilon^{(0)}=1$ and $\varepsilon^{(1)}\neq 1$, and let $\overline{\pi}=\varepsilon-1$.

nodes.name: Fields E_{Q_p} and E
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_p}=\mathbb F_p((\overline{\pi}))$, and define $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ to be a separable closure of $\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_p}$ in $\mathbb E$.

nodes.name: Galois invariants of E
nodes.statement: Then $\mathbb E$ is equipped with a continuous action of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$, and one can show that $\mathbb E^{H_{\mathbb Q_p}}=\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_p}$.

nodes.name: Witt vector rings A-tilde and B-tilde
nodes.statement:
Let $\tilde{\mathbb A}=W(\tilde{\mathbb E})$ be the ring of Witt vectors of $\tilde{\mathbb E}$ and
   \[ \tilde{\mathbb B}=\tilde{\mathbb A}[p^{-1}]=\left\{\sum_{k\gg -\infty}p^k[x_k]\mid x_k\in\tilde{\mathbb E}\right\},\]
   where $[x]$ denotes the Teichm\"uller lift of $x\in\tilde{\mathbb E}$.

nodes.name: pi, q and A_{Q_p}
nodes.statement: Let $\pi=[\varepsilon]-1$ and $q=\varphi(\pi)\slash\pi$, and define $\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q_p}$ to be the completion of $\mathbb Z_p[[\pi]][\pi^{-1}]$ in the $p$-adic topology.

nodes.name: Stability of A_{Q_p}
nodes.statement: Then $\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q_p}$ is closed under the actions of $\varphi$ and $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$, and moreover the action of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$ factors through $\Gamma_{\mathbb Q_p}$.

nodes.name: Rings B and A
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb B$ be the $p$-adic completion of the maximal unramified extension of $\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}=\mathbb A_{\mathbb Q_p}[p^{-1}]$ in $\tilde{\mathbb B}$, and let $\mathbb A=\mathbb B\cap \tilde{\mathbb A}$.

nodes.name: Ring A_F
nodes.statement: For a finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb Q_p$, put $\mathbb A_F=\mathbb A^{H_F}$.

nodes.name: Galois action on A_F
nodes.statement: If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\mathbb Q_p$, then $\mathbb A_F$ is equipped with a continuous action of $\mathcal{G}_F$ which commutes with $\varphi$.

nodes.name: (phi,Gamma)-module D_F
nodes.statement: For a $p$-adic representation $T\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Z_p}(\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p})$ (resp. $V\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Q_p}(\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p})$), define $\mathbb D_F(T)=(\mathbb A\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}T)^{H_F}$ (resp. $\mathbb D_F(V)=(\mathbb B\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}V)^{H_F}$).

nodes.name: Structure of D_F(T)
nodes.statement: Then $\mathbb D_F(T)$ (resp. $\mathbb D_F(V)$) is a free finitely generated module over $\mathbb A_F$ of rank $d=\mathrm{rank}_{\mathbb Z_p}(T)$ (resp. a finite dimensional vector space over $\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}$ of dimension $d=\dim_{\mathbb Q_p}(V)$), equipped with commuting semi-linear actions of $\varphi$ and $\Gamma_F$.
nodes.statement_short: D_F(T) is free of rank d over A_F with commuting semilinear phi and Gamma_F actions.

nodes.name: Extension of the Gamma_F-action
nodes.statement: If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\mathbb Q_p$, then the action of $\Gamma_F$ extends to an action of $G_F=\mathrm{Gal}(F_\infty\slash\mathbb Q_p)$. Moreover, the action of $G_F$ commutes with the action of $\varphi$.
nodes.label: extendaction

nodes.name: Teichmuller expansion in B-tilde
nodes.statement: Every element $x\in\tilde{\mathbb B}$ can be written uniquely of the form $x=\sum_{k\gg-\infty}p^k[x_k]$ with $x_k\in\tilde{\mathbb E}$.

nodes.name: Overconvergent rings B^{dagger,n}
nodes.statement:
For an integer $n\ge0$, define
   \[ \tilde{\mathbb B}^{\dagger,n}=\left\{ x\in\tilde{\mathbb B}\mid \lim_{k\rightarrow+\infty}\left(k+p^{-n}v_{\tilde{\mathbb E}}(x_k)\right)=+\infty\right\}\]
   and let $\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}=\tilde{\mathbb B}^{\dagger,n}\cap\mathbb B$ and $\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_F=\big(\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}\big)^{H_F}$ for any finite extension $F$ of $\mathbb Q_p$.

nodes.name: Integral overconvergent rings A^{dagger,n}
nodes.statement: Also, let $\tilde{\mathbb A}^{\dagger,n}=\{x\in\tilde{\mathbb B}^{\dagger,n}\cap\tilde{\mathbb A}\mid k+ p^{-n}v_{\tilde{\mathbb E}}(x_k)\geq 0 \hspace{1ex} \text{for all $k$}\}$, $\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}=\tilde{\mathbb A}^{\dagger,n}\cap \mathbb A$ and $\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}_F=\big(\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}\big)^{H_F}$.

nodes.name: Overconvergent rings B^dagger, A^dagger
nodes.statement: Finally, define $\mathbb B^\dagger=\bigcup_n\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}$, $\mathbb A^\dagger=\bigcup_n\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}$, $\mathbb B_F^\dagger=\bigcup_n\mathbb B_F^{\dagger,n}$ and $\mathbb A_F^\dagger=\bigcup_n\mathbb A_F^{\dagger,n}$.

nodes.name: Berger's description of A^{dagger,n}_F
nodes.statement: Explicitly, one can describe the ring $\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}_F$ for $n\gg 0$ as follows (c.f.~\cite[Proposition 1.4]{berger02}): there exists $N_F>0$ and $\pi_F\in\mathbb A^{\dagger,N_F}_F$ whose reduction mod $p$ is a uniformizer $\overline{\pi_F}$ of $\mathbb E_F$. Moreover, if $n\geq N_F$, then every element $x\in\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_F$ can be written as $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k\pi_F^k$, where the $a_k$ are elements in the maximal unramified extension $F'$ of $\mathbb Q_p$ in $F_\infty$, and where the series $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kX^k$ is holomorphic and bounded on the annulus $p^{-1/e_F p^{n-1}(p-1)}\leq\mid X\mid<1$.
nodes.statement_short: For n >= N_F, elements of B^{dagger,n}_F are Laurent series in a lift pi_F, holomorphic and bounded on an annulus.

nodes.name: Overconvergent (phi,Gamma)-modules
nodes.statement: For $V\in \mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Q_p}(\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p})$, define $\mathbb D_F^{\dagger,r}(V)=\big(\mathbb B^{\dagger,r}\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}V\big)^{H_F}$ and $\mathbb D_F^{\dagger}(V)=\big(\mathbb B^{\dagger}\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}V\big)^{H_F}$.

nodes.name: Cherbonnier-Colmez overconvergence theorem
nodes.statement:
The main result of~\cite{cherbonniercolmez98} shows that every $p$-adic representation $V$ of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$ is overconvergent, i.e. there exists $r(V)>0$ such that 
   \[ \mathbb D_{\mathbb Q_p}(V)=\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}\otimes_{\mathbb B^{\dagger,r(V)}_{\mathbb Q_p}}\mathbb D^{\dagger,r(V)}(V).\]
conclusions: every $p$-adic representation $V$ of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$ is overconvergent

nodes.name: Crystalline representations are of finite height
nodes.statement:
If $V$ is a crystalline representation of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$, then a stronger result is true: $V$ is of finite hight, i.e.  let $\tilde{\mathbb B}^+=W(\tilde{\mathbb A}^+)[p^{-1}]$, $\mathbb B^+=\mathbb B\cap\tilde{\mathbb B}^+$ and $\mathbb B^+_{\mathbb Q_p}=(\mathbb B^+)^{H_{\mathbb Q_p}}$, and define $\mathbb D^+_{\mathbb Q_p}(V)=(\mathbb B^+\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}V)^{H_{\mathbb Q_p}}$. Then
   \[ \mathbb D_{\mathbb Q_p}(V)=\mathbb D^+_{\mathbb Q_p}(V)\otimes_{\mathbb B^+_{\mathbb Q_p}}\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}.\]
assumptions: $V$ is a crystalline representation of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$

nodes.name: Ring B^+_{rig,Q_p}
nodes.statement: We write $\mathbb B_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}^+$ for the set of $f(\pi)$ where $f(X)\in\mathbb Q_p[[X]]$ converges everywhere on the open unit $p$-adic disc.

nodes.name: t = log(1+pi)
nodes.statement: In particular, $t=\log(1+\pi)\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$.

nodes.name: Robba ring
nodes.statement: For $n\ge0$, define $\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},F}$ to be the completion of $\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{F}$ in the Fr\'echet topology, and define the Robba ring $\mathbb B^{\dagger}_{\mathrm{rig},F}=\bigcup_n \mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},F}$.

nodes.name: Base change for B^{dagger,n}_{rig,F}
nodes.statement:
By \cite[Lemme~3.13]{berger02} we have 
   \[ \mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},F}=\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}\otimes_{\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathbb Q_p}}\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_F.\]

nodes.name: B^{dagger,n}_{rig,Q_p} as power series
nodes.statement:
By \cite[Proposition~I.3]{berger03}, we can identify $\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ with the ring of power series
   \[ \mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}=\big\{ f(\pi)\mid f(X)\in\mathbb Q_p\{\{X\}\} \hspace{1ex}\text{converges for $p^{-1/p^{n-1}(p-1)}\leq\mid X\mid<1$}\big\}.\]

nodes.name: phi and Gamma act on Robba rings
nodes.statement: Note that the actions of $\varphi$ and $\Gamma_F$ extend to $\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},F}$ and $\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},F}$.

nodes.name: Berger's comparison isomorphism
nodes.statement: \iota: \mathbb D^\dagger_F(V)\otimes_{\mathbb B^\dagger_F}\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},F}[t^{-1}]\cong \mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\otimes_{F^{\mathrm{nr}}}\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},F}[t^{-1}]
nodes.statement_short: Comparison isomorphism between D^dagger_F(V) and D_cris(V) after extending scalars to the Robba ring with t inverted.
nodes.label: comparison

nodes.name: Comparison isomorphism for Wach modules
nodes.statement:
If $V$ is a crystalline representation of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$, then we indeed have a comparison isomorphism
   \[
    \iota: \mathbb N(V)\otimes_{\mathbb B^+_{\mathbb Q_p}}\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}[t^{-1}]\cong \mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}[t^{-1}].
   \]
assumptions: $V$ is a crystalline representation of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$

nodes.name: Operator psi
nodes.statement: One can hence define a left inverse $\psi$ of $\varphi$ on $\mathbb A$. Explicitly, a basis of $\mathbb A$ over $\varphi(\mathbb A)$ is given by $1,1+\pi,\dots,(1+\pi)^{p-1}$. For $x\in\mathbb A$, we may write $x=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}\varphi(x_i)(1+\pi)^i$ where $x_i\in\mathbb A$. We set $\psi(x)=x_0$.

nodes.name: psi on D_F(V)
nodes.statement: If $F$ is a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $V\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Z_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$ or $\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Q_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$, then $\psi$ extends to a left inverse of $\varphi$ $\mathbb D_F(V)$.

nodes.name: G_F-action commutes with psi
nodes.statement: If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\mathbb Q_p$, then by Remark~\ref{extendaction} we have an action of $G_F$ on $\mathbb D_F(T)$ which commutes with $\varphi$ and hence with $\psi$.

nodes.name: Tate twist
nodes.statement: If $m$ is an integer and $V\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Q_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$ (resp. $T\in\mathrm{Rep}_{\mathbb Z_p}(\mathcal{G}_F)$), we denote by $V(m)$ (resp. $T(m)$) the $\mathcal{G}_F$-representations  $V\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}\mathbb Q_p\cdot e_m$ (resp. $T\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Z_p\cdot e_m$) where $\mathcal{G}_F$ acts on $e_m$ via $\chi^m$.

nodes.name: Twisting D_cris and Wach modules
nodes.statement:
In particular, we have
   \[
   \mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V(m))=\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\otimes t^{-m}e_m,\quad\mathbb N(T(m))=\mathbb N(T)\otimes\pi^{-m}e_m\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb N(V(m))=\mathbb N(V)\otimes\pi^{-m}e_m.
   \]

nodes.name: Topological generator gamma
nodes.statement: Let $\gamma$ be a topological generator of $\Gamma_F$.

nodes.name: Herr complex
nodes.statement:
For $f=\varphi$ or $\psi$, define the complex
   \[ \mathcal{C}^\bullet_{f,\gamma}\big(\mathbb D_F(T)\big): 0\rightarrow \mathbb D_F(T)\rTo^{\alpha_f}\mathbb D_F(T)\oplus\mathbb D_F(T)\rTo^{\beta_f}\mathbb D_F(T)\rightarrow 0,\]
   where $\alpha_f(x)=\big((\gamma-1)x,(f-1)x\big)$ and $\beta_f(x,y)=(f-1)x-(\gamma-1)y$.

nodes.name: Cohomology of the Herr complex
nodes.statement: Denote by $H^i\big(\mathcal{C}^\bullet_{f,\gamma}(\mathbb D_F(V))\big)$ the $i$-th cohomology group of the complex.

nodes.name: Herr's theorem
nodes.statement:
For $f=\varphi$ or $\psi$, $H^i\big(\mathcal{C}^\bullet_{f,\gamma}(\mathbb D_F(T))\big)$ is canonically isomorphic to $H^i(F,T)$. In particular, if $(x,y)\in\mathbb D_F(T)^{\oplus 2}$ satisfies $\beta_\varphi(x,y)=0$, then the corresponding cohomology class in $H^1(F,T)$ is given by the cocycle
    \[ c_{(x,y)}: \sigma\mapsto \frac{\sigma-1}{\gamma-1}x-(\sigma-1)z,\]
    where $z\in\mathbb A\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}T$ is such that $(\varphi-1)z=y$.
nodes.statement_short: The Herr complex computes Galois cohomology of T; explicit cocycle for a class in H^1.

nodes.name: Fontaine's isomorphism H^1_Iw = D(T)^{psi=1}
nodes.statement: We have an $\Lambda(\Gamma_F)$-equivariant isomorphism $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(F,T)\cong\mathbb D_{F}(T)^{\psi=1}$. If $F_\infty$ is Galois over $\mathbb Q_p$, then the isomorphism is compatible with the action of $G=\mathrm{Gal}(F_\infty\slash \mathbb Q_p)$.
conclusions: the isomorphism is compatible with the action of $G=\mathrm{Gal}(F_\infty\slash \mathbb Q_p)$
also_stated_at: If $F$ is an arbitrary finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, then $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(F,T)$ is canonically isomorphic to $\mathbb D_F(T)^{\psi=1}$, where $\mathbb D_F(T)$ denotes the $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-module of $T$ over the base field $\mathbb A_F$.
nodes.label: comp

nodes.name: Proof of PP1
nodes.statement: See \cite[Th\'eor\`eme II.1.3]{cherbonniercolmez99}.
nodes.statement_short: Cited from Cherbonnier-Colmez.

nodes.name: a_p = 0
nodes.statement: Assume throughout this section that $a_p=0$.

nodes.name: Tate module and V
nodes.statement: Let $T_p(E)$ be the Tate module of $E$ at $p$ and write $V=T_pE\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p$, so as a representation of $\mathcal{G}_{\mathbb Q_p}$, $V$ is crystalline with Hodge-Tate weights $0,1$.

nodes.name: Basis v_1, v_2 of D_cris(V)
nodes.statement: Let $v_1$ be a basis of $\mathrm{Fil}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$, and extend it to a basis $v_1,v_2$ of $\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$ such that the matrix of $\varphi$ on $\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$ in this basis is $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ p & 0\end{pmatrix}$.

nodes.name: Pollack's half logarithms log^+-
nodes.statement: Define $\log^-(1+\pi)=\prod_{i\geq 0}\frac{\varphi^{2i}(q)}{p}$ and $\log^+(1+\pi)=\prod_{i\geq 0}\frac{\varphi^{2i+1}(q)}{p}$, which are elements of $\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$.

nodes.name: Basis of the Wach module of a supersingular curve
nodes.statement:
Since the Hodge-Tate weights of $V$ are non-negative, we have 
  \[ \mathbb N(T)\subset \mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\otimes\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}\]
  by \cite[Proposition II.2.1]{berger03}, and it follows form Appendice (3) in {\em op.cit.} that a basis $n_1,n_2$ of $\mathbb N(T)$ is given by $\begin{pmatrix} n_1 \\ n_2\end{pmatrix} = M\begin{pmatrix} v_1 \\ v_2\end{pmatrix}$, where 
  \begin{equation} M= \begin{pmatrix} \log^-(1+\pi) & 0 \\ 0 & \log^+(1+\pi) \end{pmatrix}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: N(T) sits in D_cris(V) tensor B^+_rig and has basis n_1,n_2 = M(v_1,v_2) with M = diag(log^-, log^+).

nodes.name: Matrix M
nodes.statement: M= \begin{pmatrix} \log^-(1+\pi) & 0 \\ 0 & \log^+(1+\pi) \end{pmatrix}.
nodes.label: matrixM

nodes.name: Coordinates x_i and x_i'
nodes.statement:
For $x\in \mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$, we write 
  \[x=x_1v_1+x_2v_2=x_1'n_1+x_2'n_2\] 
  with $x_i\in\mathbb B^{\dagger,N}_{\mathrm{rig},K}$ and $x_i'\in \mathbb A^{\dagger,N}_{K}$.

nodes.name: Base change of coordinates
nodes.statement: x_1=x_1'\log^-(1+\pi)\quad\text{and}\quad x_2=x_2'\log^+(1+\pi).
nodes.label: basechange

nodes.name: Signed Iwasawa cohomology H^1_Iw(K,T)^i
nodes.statement:
For $i=1,2$, let 
   \[ H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i=\left\{x\in\mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}:\varphi(x_i)=-p\psi(x_i)\right\}.\]
   For $n\geq 1$, define $H^1(K_n,T)^i$ to be the image of $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$ under the natural projection map $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)\rightarrow H^1(K_n,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Elements x of D^dagger_K(T)^{psi=1} with phi(x_i) = -p psi(x_i), and their projections to H^1(K_n,T).

nodes.name: Signed cohomology as kernel of Coleman maps
nodes.label: relationtoColeman

nodes.name: Signed local condition H^1_{f,i}(K_n)
nodes.statement:
Let $H^1_{f,i}(K_n,E_{p^\infty})$ be the orthogonal complement of $H^1(K_n,T)^i$ under the Pontryagin duality
   \[ [\sim,\sim]: H^1(K_n,T)\times H^1(K_n,E_{p^\infty})\rTo \mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p\]
   for $i=1,2$.

nodes.name: Completions L_nu
nodes.statement:
For a prime $
u$ of $L$, denote by $L_
u$ be the completion of $L$ at $
u$, and let $L_{
u,n}=L_
u(\mu_{p^n})$.

nodes.name: Set of primes S
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be the finite set of primes of $\mathbb Q$ containing $p$, all the primes where $E$ has bad reduction and the infinite prime.
also_stated_at: As above, let $S$ be the finite set of primes of $\mathbb Q$ containing $p$, all the primes where $E$ has bad reduction and the infinite prime.

nodes.name: Local quotients J^i_v(L_n)
nodes.statement:
For all $v\in S$, define 
   \[ J^i_v(L_n)= \bigoplus_{w_n\mid v}  \frac{H^1(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})}{H^1_{f,i}(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})},\] 
   where the direct sum is taken over all primes $w_n$ of $L_n$ above $v$ and $H^1_{f,i}(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})=H^1_f(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})$ whenever $v\neq p$.

nodes.name: J^i_v(L_infty)
nodes.statement: We write $J^i_v(L_\infty)=\varinjlim J^i_v(L_n)$.

nodes.name: Signed Selmer group Sel^i(E/L_infty)
nodes.statement:
For $i=1,2$, define 
    \[ \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_\infty)=\ker\left( H^1(G_S(L_\infty),E_{p^\infty})\rTo \bigoplus_{v\in S}J^i_v(L_\infty)\right).\]

nodes.name: Signed Selmer group at finite level
nodes.statement:
For $n\geq 0$, we also define
    \[ \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_n)=\ker\left( H^1(G_S(L_n),E_{p^\infty})\rTo \bigoplus_{v\in S}J^i_v(L_{n,v})\right).\]

nodes.name: Sel^i(E/L_infty) is the direct limit
nodes.statement:
Taking direct limits then gives
    \[\mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_\infty)=\varinjlim \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_n).\]

nodes.name: Bases nu-bar and n-bar
nodes.statement: Let $\bar{\nu}_1,\bar{\nu}_2$ and $\bar{n}_1,\bar{n}_2$ be the bases of $\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V(-1))$ and $\mathbb N(V(-1))$, respectively, as defined in \cite[\S 3.2]{leiloefflerzerbes10}.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Formal group E-hat and V-hat
nodes.statement: In particular, if $\hat{E}$ denotes the formal group of $E$ and $\hat{V}=T_p\hat{E}\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p$, then $\bar{\nu}_1$ is a basis vector of $\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(\hat{V}(-1))$ and $\bar{n}_1=\bar{\nu}_1$ is a basis of $\mathbb N(\hat{V}(-1))$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Change of basis matrix M'
nodes.statement:
If $M'$ is the change of basis matrix with 
    \begin{equation} \begin{pmatrix}\bar{\nu}_1\\\bar{\nu}_2\end{pmatrix}=M'\begin{pmatrix}\bar{n}_1\\\bar{n}_2\end{pmatrix},
    \end{equation}
    then $M'$ is lower triangular, with $1$ and $\frac{t}{\pi}$ on the diagonal.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
assumptions: $M'$ is the change of basis matrix
conclusions: $M'$ is lower triangular, with $1$ and $\frac{t}{\pi}$ on the diagonal

nodes.name: Change of basis
nodes.statement: \begin{pmatrix}\bar{\nu}_1\\\bar{\nu}_2\end{pmatrix}=M'\begin{pmatrix}\bar{n}_1\\\bar{n}_2\end{pmatrix},
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.label: matrix

nodes.name: Coordinates in the n-bar basis
nodes.statement: If $x\in\mathbb N(V)$, then there exist unique $x_1,x_2\in\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+$ such that $x=(x_1\bar{n}_1+x_2\bar{n}_2)\otimes\pi^{-1}e_1$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Coordinates in the nu-bar basis
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{matrix}, we can find unique $x_1',x_2'\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ such that
    \begin{equation} x=(x_1'\bar{\nu}_1+x_2'\bar{\nu}_2)\otimes t^{-1}e_1
    \end{equation}
    with $x_2'=x_2$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Second form of x
nodes.statement: x=(x_1'\bar{\nu}_1+x_2'\bar{\nu}_2)\otimes t^{-1}e_1
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.label: secondform

nodes.name: Frobenius matrix P is upper triangular
nodes.statement: If $P$ denotes the matrix of $\varphi$ with respect to the basis $\bar{n}_1,\bar{n}_2$, then $P$ is upper-triangular.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Shape of the Frobenius matrix P
nodes.statement:
Let $\alpha$ be the unit root of the polynomial $X^2-a_pX+p$, then $P$ is in fact of the form
    \[ P=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \star \\
         0 & uq
        \end{pmatrix}\]
    for some $u\in (\mathbb B^+_{\mathbb Q_p})^\times$ which is congruent to $\alpha^{-1}\mod \pi$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: With alpha the unit root of X^2-a_pX+p, P = [[alpha, *],[0, uq]] with u a unit congruent to alpha^{-1} mod pi.

nodes.name: Coleman maps
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Coleman maps Col_i and underline-Col_i on N(V)^{psi=1}, characterised by an expansion of (1-phi)(x) in the nu-bar basis.

nodes.name: Coleman map identity

nodes.name: Ordinary signed local conditions over Q_{p,n}
nodes.statement: Let $H^1(\mathbb Q_{p,n},T)^i$ be the image of $\ker(\underline{\mathrm{Col}}_i)\cap\mathbb N(T)^{\psi=1}$ under the natural maps $\mathbb N(T)^{\psi=1}\rightarrow H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)\rightarrow H^1(\mathbb Q_{p,n},T)$ and write $H^1_{f,i}(\mathbb Q_{p,n},E_{p^\infty})$ for the exact annihilator of $H^1(\mathbb Q_{p,n},T)^i$ under the Tate pairing.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Ordinary signed Selmer groups over Q(mu_{p^n})
nodes.statement:
Define
     \[
     \mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))=\ker\left(\mathrm{Sel}(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rightarrow \frac{H^1(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),E_{p^\infty})}{H^1_{f,i}(\mathbb Q_p(\mu_{p^n}),E_{p^\infty})})\right)
     \]
     where $\mathrm{Sel}(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))$ denotes the usual Selmer group and we define $\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^\infty}))$ to be the direct limit of $\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups

nodes.name: Normalised basis with u = alpha^{-1}
nodes.statement: We can choose $\bar{n}_2$ such that $u=\alpha^{-1}$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.label: basis

nodes.name: Proof of PP2
nodes.statement:
If we let $\bar{n}_1'=\bar{n}_1$ and $\bar{n}_2'=v\bar{n}_2$ where $v\in(\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+)^\times$, then $\bar{n}_1',\bar{n}_2'$ is also a basis of $\mathbb N(V(-1))$. The matrix of $\varphi$ with respect to this basis is of the form
    \[ P'=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \star \\
          0 & v^{-1}\varphi(v)uq
         \end{pmatrix}.\]
    Note that $\alpha u\equiv1\mod\pi$ implies that $\varphi^n(\alpha u)\rightarrow 1$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the product $\prod_{n\ge0}\varphi^n(\alpha u)$ converges to an element $u'\in(\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+)^\times$. Since $u'\varphi(u')^{-1}=\alpha u$, we deduce that $P'$ is of the required form if we take $v=u'$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Rescale n-bar_2 by an infinite product converging since alpha u = 1 mod pi.

nodes.name: PP2 step 1
nodes.statement:
If we let $\bar{n}_1'=\bar{n}_1$ and $\bar{n}_2'=v\bar{n}_2$ where $v\in(\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+)^\times$, then $\bar{n}_1',\bar{n}_2'$ is also a basis of $\mathbb N(V(-1))$. The matrix of $\varphi$ with respect to this basis is of the form
    \[ P'=\begin{pmatrix} \alpha & \star \\
          0 & v^{-1}\varphi(v)uq
         \end{pmatrix}.\]
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Rescale n-bar_2 by a unit v and compute the new Frobenius matrix.

nodes.name: PP2 step 2
nodes.statement: Note that $\alpha u\equiv1\mod\pi$ implies that $\varphi^n(\alpha u)\rightarrow 1$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. In particular, the product $\prod_{n\ge0}\varphi^n(\alpha u)$ converges to an element $u'\in(\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+)^\times$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: The product of phi^n(alpha u) converges to a unit u'.

nodes.name: PP2 step 3
nodes.statement: Since $u'\varphi(u')^{-1}=\alpha u$, we deduce that $P'$ is of the required form if we take $v=u'$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Take v=u'.

nodes.name: Kernel of Col_2 in the n-bar basis
nodes.statement:
With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis},
   \[
   \ker(\underline{\mathrm{Col}}_2)=\left\{x\in\mathbb N(V)^{\psi=1}|\varphi(x_2)=\alpha x_2\text{ where }x=(x_1\bar{n}_1+x_2\bar{n}_2)\otimes \pi^{-1}e_1\text{ with } x_i\in\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+\right\}.
   \]
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
assumptions: With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis}
conclusions:
\[
   \ker(\underline{\mathrm{Col}}_2)=\left\{x\in\mathbb N(V)^{\psi=1}|\varphi(x_2)=\alpha x_2\text{ where }x=(x_1\bar{n}_1+x_2\bar{n}_2)\otimes \pi^{-1}e_1\text{ with } x_i\in\mathbb B_{\mathbb Q_p}^+\right\}.
   \]
nodes.statement_short: ker(Col_2) consists of x in N(V)^{psi=1} whose second n-bar coordinate satisfies phi(x_2) = alpha x_2.
nodes.label: firstform

nodes.name: Proof of PP3
nodes.statement: By \eqref{colemanmaps}, we have $\mathrm{Col}_2(x)=\alpha x_2-\varphi(x_2)$. Moreover, $M$ is lower triangular with $\alpha\frac{t}{\pi q}$ and $\alpha^{-1}$ on the diagonal. Therefore, $\ker(\underline{\mathrm{Col}}_2)=\ker(\mathrm{Col}_2)$ and we are done.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Compute Col_2 from the Coleman map identity and use triangularity of M.

nodes.name: PP3 step 1
nodes.statement: By \eqref{colemanmaps}, we have $\mathrm{Col}_2(x)=\alpha x_2-\varphi(x_2)$.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Compute Col_2(x) from the Coleman map identity.

nodes.name: PP3 step 2
nodes.statement: Moreover, $M$ is lower triangular with $\alpha\frac{t}{\pi q}$ and $\alpha^{-1}$ on the diagonal.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: M is lower triangular with unit entry alpha^{-1}.

nodes.name: PP3 step 3
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\ker(\underline{\mathrm{Col}}_2)=\ker(\mathrm{Col}_2)$ and we are done.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Conclude the kernels agree.

nodes.name: Kernel of Col_2 in the nu-bar basis
nodes.statement:
With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis},
   \[
   \ker(\underline{\mathrm{Col}}_2)=\left\{x\in\mathbb N(V)^{\psi=1}|\varphi(x_2)=\alpha x_2\text{ where }x=(x_1\bar{\nu}_1+x_2\bar{\nu}_2)\otimes t^{-1}e_1 \text{ with } x_i\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}\right\}.
   \]
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
assumptions: With respect to the basis given by Lemma~\ref{basis}
nodes.statement_short: Same description of ker(Col_2) using coordinates in the nu-bar basis over B^+_rig.
nodes.label: description

nodes.name: Proof of PP4
nodes.statement: This follows from Lemma~\ref{firstform} and \eqref{secondform}.
nodes.section: 3.2.1 Coleman maps and signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemma 3.8 with the second form of x.

nodes.name: Ordinary signed Selmer group Sel^2(E/L_infty)
nodes.statement:
For all $v\in S$, define 
   \[ J^2_v(L_n)= \bigoplus_{w_n\mid v}  \frac{H^1(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})}{H^1_{f,2}(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})},\] 
   where the direct sum is taken over all primes $w_n$ of $L_n$ above $v$. Here, $H^1_{f,2}(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})=H^1_f(L_{w_n,n},E_{p^\infty})$ whenever $v\nmid p$. Define $J^{2}_v(L_\infty)=\varinjlim J^{(2)}_v(L_n)$. Define
   \[ \mathrm{Sel}^2(E\slash L_\infty)=\ker\left( H^1(G_S(L_\infty),E_{p^\infty})\rightarrow \bigoplus_{v\in S}J^2_v(L_\infty)\right).\]

nodes.name: No nonzero solutions of phi(x) = a x
nodes.statement:
Let $a\in \mathbb Z_p^\times$, and assume that $a$ is not a root of unity. If $x\in\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},K}$ satisfies 
    \begin{equation} a x-\varphi(x)=0
    \end{equation}
    then $x=0$.
assumptions: assume that $a$ is not a root of unity
nodes.label: onlytrivialsolution

nodes.name: phi(x) = a x
nodes.statement: a x-\varphi(x)=0
nodes.label: nosolution

nodes.name: Proof of PP5
nodes.statement:
If $x\in \mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, then we can substitute $\pi=e^t-1$ to write $x$ of the form $\sum_{n\geq 0}c_nt^n$ with $c_n\in\mathbb Q_p$. Since $\varphi(t)=pt$, it is clear from this description that for any $a
eq 1$ and $x
e0$, we have $\varphi(x)
eq ax$. 
    
    Let $x\in\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}-\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$. Assume that there exists $n\ge 0$ be such that $x\in \mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ and $x
ot\in \mathbb B^{\dagger,n-1}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$. Then $\varphi(x)\in \mathbb B^{\dagger,n+1}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}-\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, so $\varphi(x)
eq a x$.
    
    If $x\in\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ for all $n\ge0$ and $x
ot\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, then $\varphi^{-1}(x)$ converges in $\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{dR}}$, so if we write $x=f(\pi)$, then $f(T)$ does not have a pole at $\varepsilon^{(1)}-1$. But $f(T)$ has a pole at $T=0$ as $x
ot\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, so $f ig( (T+1)^p-1 ig)$ has poles at the $\{(\varepsilon^{(1)})^i-1:0\leq i<p\}$. Hence $\varphi(x)
eq ax$.
    
    Assume now that $x\in \mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},K}$ satisfies $\varphi(x)=ax$, and that $x
ot\in \mathbb B^{\dagger}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$. On replacing $K$ by its Galois closure, if necessary, we may assume that $K\slash\mathbb Q_p$, and hence $K_{\infty}\slash\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}$, are Galois. Let $H=\mathrm{Gal}(K_{\infty}\slash \mathbb Q_{p,\infty})$. Since $\varphi$ is $H$-equivariant, $\sigma(x)$ also satisfies~\eqref{nosolution} for all $\sigma\in H$. More generally, if $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_i\in H$, then $y=\sigma_1(x_2)\dots\sigma_i(x_2)$ satisfies $a^iy=\varphi(y)$. The coefficients of the polynomial
    \[ f(Y)=\prod_{\sigma\in H} (Y-\sigma(x))\]
    are elements in $\mathbb B^{\dagger}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ which satisfy an equation of the form~\eqref{nosolution}, so they must all be zero by the above argument. But the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ divides $f(Y)$, which gives a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on where x lies in the Robba ring; for general K use Galois conjugates and the minimal polynomial to reduce to Q_p.

nodes.name: PP5 step 1
nodes.statement:
If $x\in \mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, then we can substitute $\pi=e^t-1$ to write $x$ of the form $\sum_{n\geq 0}c_nt^n$ with $c_n\in\mathbb Q_p$. Since $\varphi(t)=pt$, it is clear from this description that for any $a
eq 1$ and $x
e0$, we have $\varphi(x)
eq ax$.
nodes.statement_short: Case x in B^+_rig: expand in powers of t.

nodes.name: PP5 step 2
nodes.statement: Let $x\in\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}-\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$. Assume that there exists $n\ge 0$ be such that $x\in \mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ and $x\not\in \mathbb B^{\dagger,n-1}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$. Then $\varphi(x)\in \mathbb B^{\dagger,n+1}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}-\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, so $\varphi(x)\neq a x$.
nodes.statement_short: Case x of exact level n: phi raises the level.

nodes.name: PP5 step 3
nodes.statement:
If $x\in\mathbb B^{\dagger,n}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ for all $n\ge0$ and $x
ot\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, then $\varphi^{-1}(x)$ converges in $\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{dR}}$, so if we write $x=f(\pi)$, then $f(T)$ does not have a pole at $\varepsilon^{(1)}-1$. But $f(T)$ has a pole at $T=0$ as $x
ot\in\mathbb B^+_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$, so $f ig( (T+1)^p-1 ig)$ has poles at the $\{(\varepsilon^{(1)})^i-1:0\leq i<p\}$. Hence $\varphi(x)
eq ax$.
nodes.statement_short: Case x in all levels but not in B^+: compare poles.

nodes.name: PP5 step 4
nodes.statement: Assume now that $x\in \mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},K}$ satisfies $\varphi(x)=ax$, and that $x\not\in \mathbb B^{\dagger}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$. On replacing $K$ by its Galois closure, if necessary, we may assume that $K\slash\mathbb Q_p$, and hence $K_{\infty}\slash\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}$, are Galois.
nodes.statement_short: General K: reduce to K/Q_p Galois.

nodes.name: PP5 step 5
nodes.statement: Let $H=\mathrm{Gal}(K_{\infty}\slash \mathbb Q_{p,\infty})$. Since $\varphi$ is $H$-equivariant, $\sigma(x)$ also satisfies~\eqref{nosolution} for all $\sigma\in H$. More generally, if $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_i\in H$, then $y=\sigma_1(x_2)\dots\sigma_i(x_2)$ satisfies $a^iy=\varphi(y)$.
nodes.statement_short: Galois conjugates and their products satisfy similar equations.

nodes.name: PP5 step 6
nodes.statement:
The coefficients of the polynomial
    \[ f(Y)=\prod_{\sigma\in H} (Y-\sigma(x))\]
    are elements in $\mathbb B^{\dagger}_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ which satisfy an equation of the form~\eqref{nosolution}, so they must all be zero by the above argument.
nodes.statement_short: Coefficients of prod (Y - sigma(x)) vanish by the Q_p case.

nodes.name: PP5 step 7
nodes.statement: But the minimal polynomial of $x$ over $\mathbb B^\dagger_{\mathrm{rig},\mathbb Q_p}$ divides $f(Y)$, which gives a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: Contradiction with the minimal polynomial.

nodes.name: alpha is not a root of unity
nodes.statement: The unit root $\alpha$ of the polynomial $X^2-a_pX+p$ is a Weil number of complex absolute value $\sqrt{p}$, so it cannot be a root of unity.
nodes.label: Weilnumber

Proof of PP6

nodes.statement: $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^2$ if and only if $x\in \mathbb D_{K}(\hat{T})^{\psi=1}$.
conclusions: $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^2$ if and only if $x\in \mathbb D_{K}(\hat{T})^{\psi=1}$.

nodes.name: Proof of PP7
nodes.statement: It follows immediately from the comparison isomorphism and the fact that $\bar{\nu}_1=\bar{n}_1$ that any $x\in\mathbb D_{K}(T)^{\psi=1}$ which satisfies $\iota(x)=x_1\bar{\nu}_1\otimes t^{-1}e_1$ must indeed lie in $\mathbb D_{K}(\hat{T})$.
nodes.statement_short: Comparison isomorphism plus nu-bar_1 = n-bar_1.

nodes.name: Sel^2 equals the usual Selmer group (ordinary case)
nodes.statement: We have $\mathrm{Sel}(E\slash L_\infty)=\mathrm{Sel}^2(E\slash L_\infty)$.
also_stated_at: If $E$ has good ordinary reduction at $p$, then Theorem~\ref{sameSelmergroup} shows that $\mathrm{Sel}^2(E\slash L_\infty)$ agrees with the usual Selmer group $\mathrm{Sel}(E\slash L_\infty)$.

To justify the proposed definition of signed Selmer groups over $K_\infty$, we show in Section~\ref{ordinary} that on extending our construction to the good ordinary case, $\mathrm{Sel}^2(E\slash K_\infty)$ again agrees with the usual Selmer group $\mathrm{Sel}(E\slash K_\infty)$ for any finite extension $K$ of $\mathbb Q$.
nodes.label: sameSelmergroup

nodes.name: Proof of PP8
nodes.statement:
Since $L/\mathbb Q$ is finite and $E$ had good ordinary reduction at $p$, we have $V^{H_{L_
u}}=0$ for all primes $
u$ of $L$ above $p$. This implies that 
    \[
     H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(L_
u,\hat{T})\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p=\lim_{\leftarrow} H^1_g(L_{
u,n},T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p
    \]
    by \cite[Proposition~0.1]{perrinriou00a} (or \cite[Theorem~A]{berger05}). But $H^1_f(L_{
u,n},T)=H^1_g(L_{
u,n},T)$ by \cite[(3.11.2)]{blochkato90}), we have 
    \[
     H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(L_
u,\hat{T})\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p=\lim_{\leftarrow} H^1_f(L_{
u,n},T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p.
    \]
     
    It is clear that the quotients $\mathbb D_K(T)^{\psi=1}\slash\mathbb D_{K}(\hat{T})^{\psi=1}$ and $H^1(L_{
u,n},T)\slash H^1_f(L_{
u,n},T)$ are torsion-free over $\mathbb Z_p$. We can therefore deduce that 
    \[
     H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(L_
u,\hat{T})=\lim_{\leftarrow} H^1_f(L_{
u,n},T).
    \]
    On taking Pontryagin duals, we have $J_
u^2(L_\infty)=J_
u(L_\infty)$, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Identify H^1_Iw(L_nu, T-hat) with the inverse limit of Bloch-Kato H^1_f via Perrin-Riou/Berger, then dualise.

nodes.name: PP8 step 1
nodes.statement: Since $L/\mathbb Q$ is finite and $E$ had good ordinary reduction at $p$, we have $V^{H_{L_\nu}}=0$ for all primes $\nu$ of $L$ above $p$.
nodes.statement_short: V has no invariants under H_{L_nu}.

nodes.name: PP8 step 2

This implies that 
    \[
     H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(L_\nu,\hat{T})\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p=\lim_{\leftarrow} H^1_g(L_{\nu,n},T)\otimes_{\mathbb Z_p}\mathbb Q_p
    \]
    by \cite[Proposition~0.1]{perrinriou00a} (or \cite[Theorem~A]{berger05}).
nodes.statement_short: Identify H^1_Iw(L_nu, T-hat) rationally with lim H^1_g by Perrin-Riou/Berger.

nodes.name: PP8 step 3

nodes.statement: On taking Pontryagin duals, we have $J_\nu^2(L_\infty)=J_\nu(L_\infty)$, which finishes the proof.

nodes.name: Maximal unramified subextension K'
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, and let $K'$ be the maximal unramified extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ contained in $K_\infty$.

nodes.name: A^{dagger,n}_K is p-adically complete
nodes.statement: It is easy to see from the description of the ring $\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}_K$ given in Section~\ref{overcon} that it is complete in the $p$-adic topology.

nodes.name: A^{dagger,n}_K as a p-adic completion
nodes.statement: For all $n\geq N_K$, $\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}_K$ is the $p$-adic completion of $\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]\cap\mathbb A^{\dagger,n}_K$.
nodes.label: completion

nodes.name: Proof of PP9
nodes.statement:
Note that the condition that $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kX^k$ is holomorphic and bounded above by $1$ on the annulus $p^{-1/e_Kp^{n-1}(p-1)}\leq\mid X\mid<1$ is equivalent to the condition that
   \[ v_p(a_k)+\frac{k}{e_K(p-1)p^{n-1}}\geq 0 \hspace{2ex} \text{and $\rightarrow +\infty$ as $k\rightarrow -\infty$}.\]
nodes.statement_short: Translate holomorphy and boundedness on the annulus into valuation conditions on coefficients.

nodes.name: Vanishing at infinitely many levels
nodes.statement: Let $x\in\mathbb A^{\dagger,N}_K$ where $N\ge N_K$. If $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x)=0$ for infinitely many $n\ge N$, then $x=0$.
nodes.label: vanish

nodes.name: Proof of PP10
nodes.statement:
Firstly, we assume that $x\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]$. We write $\sigma$ for the Frobenious in $\mathrm{Gal}(K'/\mathbb Q_p)$. Let
   \[
   F(X)=\sum_{m\ge -r}b_mX^m\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![X]\!][X^{-1}]
   \]
   such that $F(\pi_K)=x$. For $i=1,\ldots,[K':\mathbb Q_p]$, write 
   \[ F_i(X)=\sum_{m\ge -r}\sigma^i(b_m)X^m.\]
   Then $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x)=F_i(\pi_{n})$, where $i+n\equiv0\mod[K':\mathbb Q_p]$ and $\pi_n=\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(\pi_K)$. Therefore, there exists an $i$ such that $F_i$ has infinitely many zeros. But $F_i\in X^{-r}\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![X]\!]$, so $F_i=0$ by the Weierstrass preparation theorem. This implies that $b_m=0$ for all $m$, so $x=0$. 

   To conclude, note that if $n\ge N$, $\{x\in\mathbb A^{\dagger,N}_K:\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x)=0\}$ is a closed set of $\mathbb A^{\dagger,N}_K$ under the $p$-adic topology and $\mathbb A^{\dagger,N}_K$ is the $p$-adic completion of $\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]\cap\mathbb A^{\dagger,N}_K$ by Lemma~\ref{completion}.
nodes.statement_short: Weierstrass preparation for Laurent series in pi_K, then density via Lemma 4.1.

nodes.name: PP10 step 1
nodes.statement: Firstly, we assume that $x\in\mathcal{O}_{K'}[\![\pi_K]\!][\pi_K^{-1}]$.

nodes.name: Compatibility of trace with theta o phi^{-n}
nodes.statement:
Let $n\gg0$ and $x\in\mathbb B_{K}^{\dagger,n}$, then
   \[
    \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ \theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x)=\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}(x).
   \]
nodes.label: comptrace

nodes.name: Proof of PP11
nodes.statement:
We let $n$ be an integer such that $[K_n:K_{n-1}]=p$ and $n\ge a(K)+1$ where $a(K)$ is the integer as in \cite[Proposition~III.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}. Write
   \[
    x=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}[\varepsilon]^i\varphi(x_i)
   \]
   where $x_i\in\mathbb B_{K}^{\dagger,n-1}$. Then,
   \[
    \theta\circ\varphi^{-n+1}(x_i)\in K_{n-1}
   \]
   for all $i$. Therefore,
   \begin{eqnarray*}
    \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ \theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x)&=&\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\left(\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}\zeta_{p^n}^i\theta\circ\varphi^{1-n}(x_i)\right)\\
    &=&p\theta\circ\varphi^{1-n}(x_0).
   \end{eqnarray*}
   But we have $\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}(x)=p\varphi(x_0)$, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Expand x in the basis [epsilon]^i over phi(B) and compute the trace termwise.

nodes.name: PP11 step 1
nodes.statement:
We let $n$ be an integer such that $[K_n:K_{n-1}]=p$ and $n\ge a(K)+1$ where $a(K)$ is the integer as in \cite[Proposition~III.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}. Write
   \[
    x=\sum_{i=0}^{p-1}[\varepsilon]^i\varphi(x_i)
   \]
   where $x_i\in\mathbb B_{K}^{\dagger,n-1}$.

nodes.name: PP11 step 2
nodes.statement:
Then,
   \[
    \theta\circ\varphi^{-n+1}(x_i)\in K_{n-1}
   \]
   for all $i$.

nodes.statement: But we have $\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}(x)=p\varphi(x_0)$, which finishes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Match with the trace on B.

nodes.name: D^dagger_K(T) from the Wach module
nodes.statement:
It is clear from the definition that
  \[ \mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)=\mathbb A^\dagger_K\otimes_{\mathbb A^+_{\mathbb Q_p}}\mathbb N(T),\]
  so in particular the basis $n_1,n_2$ of $\mathbb N(T)$ given in Section~\ref{supersingular} is a basis of $\mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)$ over $\mathbb A^\dagger_K$.

nodes.name: psi=1 part is overconvergent of level N
nodes.statement:
As shown in \cite[Proposition III.3.2]{cherbonniercolmez99}, we have 
  $\mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}\subset \mathbb D^{\dagger,N}_K(T)$  for $N\ge N(K,V)$.

nodes.name: Fixed level N
nodes.statement: Fix such an $N$; note that it is not uniquely defined.

nodes.name: Trace relations for x_1 and x_2
nodes.statement:
Let $x\in \mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$, then
   \[\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_1)=-\theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_1)\]
   for all odd integers $n\ge N+2$ and
   \[\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_2)=-\theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_2)\]
   for all even integers $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Trace of theta o phi^{-n}(x_i) equals -theta o phi^{2-n}(x_i) for odd n (i=1) or even n (i=2), n >= N+2.
nodes.label: triv0

nodes.name: Proof of PP12
nodes.statement:
By definitions, we have $\varphi(\log^+(1+\pi))=\frac{p}{q}\log^-(1+\pi)$ and $\varphi(\log^-(1+\pi))=\log^+(1+\pi)$, and that similar relations hold when replacing $\varphi$ by $\psi$. The relations \eqref{basechange} therefore imply that
   \begin{eqnarray}
    \varphi(x_1)+p\psi(x_1)&=&\left(\varphi(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')\right)\log^+(1+\pi); \\
    \varphi(x_2)+p\psi(x_2)&=&\left(\varphi(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')\right)p/q\log^-(1+\pi). \end{eqnarray}
   If $n\ge 2$ is an even integer, then $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}\left(\log^+(1+\pi)\right)=0$. Therefore, \eqref{log1} implies that
   \[
   \theta\circ\varphi^{-n+1}(x_1)+\theta\circ\varphi^{-n-1}\left(p\varphi\circ\psi(x_1)\right)=0.
   \] 
   Recall that $p\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}$, so Lemma~\ref{comptrace} implies the first part of the lemma. Similarly, the second half the lemma follows from \eqref{log2} and the fact that 
   \[\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}\left(p/q\log^-(1+\pi)\right)=0\]
   for all odd integers $n\ge 3$.
nodes.statement_short: Use phi-relations between log^+ and log^-, their vanishing at alternate levels, and Lemma 4.3.

nodes.name: PP12 step 1
nodes.statement: By definitions, we have $\varphi(\log^+(1+\pi))=\frac{p}{q}\log^-(1+\pi)$ and $\varphi(\log^-(1+\pi))=\log^+(1+\pi)$, and that similar relations hold when replacing $\varphi$ by $\psi$.
nodes.statement_short: Frobenius relations between log^+ and log^-.

nodes.name: PP12 step 2
nodes.statement_short: Derive relations (9) and (10).

nodes.statement: \varphi(x_1)+p\psi(x_1)&=&\left(\varphi(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')\right)\log^+(1+\pi);

If $n\ge 2$ is an even integer, then $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}\left(\log^+(1+\pi)\right)=0$. Therefore, \eqref{log1} implies that
   \[
   \theta\circ\varphi^{-n+1}(x_1)+\theta\circ\varphi^{-n-1}\left(p\varphi\circ\psi(x_1)\right)=0.
   \]

nodes.statement: Recall that $p\varphi\circ\psi=\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}$, so Lemma~\ref{comptrace} implies the first part of the lemma.

Similarly, the second half the lemma follows from \eqref{log2} and the fact that

   for all odd integers $n\ge 3$.

nodes.name: Trace characterisation of H^1_Iw(K,T)^i
nodes.statement:
Let $x\in \mathbb D^\dagger_K(T)^{\psi=1}$, then $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$ if and only if
   \[\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_i)\]
   for all $n\ge N+2$.
conclusions:
$x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$ if and only if
   \[\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_i)\]
   for all $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.label: des1

nodes.name: Proof of PP13
nodes.statement:
If $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$, then 
   \[
   \varphi^2(x_i)=-p\varphi\circ\psi(x_i)=-\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}(x_i).
   \]
   On applying $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}$ to both sides, we have by Lemma~\ref{comptrace} that
   \[
   \theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_i)=-\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_i)
   \]
   as required.

   Conversely, we assume that 
   \[
   \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_i)
   \]
   for all $n\ge N+2$. Then $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}\left(\varphi(x_i)+p\psi(x_i)\right)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{comptrace}. Our assumption implies that $\varphi(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')=0$ for $i=1$ and $\varphi(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')=0$ for $i=2$ by Lemma~\ref{vanish} and the equations \eqref{log1} and \eqref{log2}. Therefore, we have $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$ as required.
nodes.statement_short: Forward: apply theta o phi^{-n} and Lemma 4.3. Converse: Lemma 4.2 forces the relations (9), (10) to vanish.

nodes.name: PP13 step 1
nodes.statement:
If $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$, then 
   \[
   \varphi^2(x_i)=-p\varphi\circ\psi(x_i)=-\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb B/\varphi(\mathbb B)}(x_i).
   \]
nodes.statement_short: Forward direction: rewrite the defining relation via the trace.

nodes.name: PP13 step 2
nodes.statement:
On applying $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}$ to both sides, we have by Lemma~\ref{comptrace} that
   \[
   \theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_i)=-\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_i)
   \]
   as required.
nodes.statement_short: Apply theta o phi^{-n} and Lemma 4.3.

nodes.name: PP13 step 3
nodes.statement:
Conversely, we assume that 
   \[
   \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_i)=-\theta\circ\varphi^{2-n}(x_i)
   \]
   for all $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Converse: assume the trace relations.

nodes.statement: Then $\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}\left(\varphi(x_i)+p\psi(x_i)\right)=0$ by Lemma~\ref{comptrace}.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.3 gives vanishing at all levels.

nodes.statement: Our assumption implies that $\varphi(x_1')+\psi(qx_1')=0$ for $i=1$ and $\varphi(x_2')+q\psi(x_2')=0$ for $i=2$ by Lemma~\ref{vanish} and the equations \eqref{log1} and \eqref{log2}.

nodes.statement: Therefore, we have $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i$ as required.

nodes.name: Rewriting of Proposition 4.5
Description of H^1_Iw(K,T)^i via dual exponential
nodes.statement_short: x lies in H^1_Iw(K,T)^i iff exp* of its image at level n lies in K_{n-1} v_1 for all n >= N+1 of the right parity.
nodes.label: trace

nodes.name: Proof of PP14
nodes.statement:
By \cite[Th\'eor\`eme IV.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}, 
   \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n}(x)= \partial_V\circ \varphi^{-n}(x)\]
   for all $n\geq N$. Since
   \[ \partial_V\circ \varphi^{-n}(x)=\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_1)\varphi^{-n}(v_1)+\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_2)\varphi^{-n}(v_2)\]
    and the image of $\exp^*_{K_n}$ lies in $K_n\otimes{\mathrm{Fil}}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$, it follows that 
   \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n}(x)=
    \begin{cases}
    (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\varphi^{-2m}(x_1)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m\ge N$}, \\
    (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\varphi^{-(2m+1)}(x_2)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m+1\ge N$}.
    \end{cases}
   \]
   Extend the trace map $\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}$ to the map $\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\mathrm{id}$ on $K_n\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$. Then, $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^1$ if and only if
   \[
   \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n}(x)=p^{-1}\exp^*_{K_{n-2}}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},{n-2}}(x)
   \]
   for all even $n\ge N+2$. But 
   \[
   \mathrm{Tr}_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}}\circ \exp^*_{K_{m}} =\exp^*_{K_{m-1}}\circ {\mathrm{cor}}_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}}
   \]
   for all $m\ge0$, so we deduce that $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^1$ if and only if
   \[
   \exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n-1}(x)=p^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}_{K_{n-1}/K_{n-2}}\circ\exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n-1}(x)
   \]
   for all even $n\ge N-2$.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit reciprocity of Cherbonnier-Colmez expresses exp* via theta o phi^{-n}; then compare traces.

nodes.name: PP14 step 1
nodes.statement:
By \cite[Th\'eor\`eme IV.2.1]{cherbonniercolmez99}, 
   \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n}(x)= \partial_V\circ \varphi^{-n}(x)\]
   for all $n\geq N$.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit reciprocity: exp* o h^1 = partial_V o phi^{-n}.

nodes.name: PP14 step 2
nodes.statement:
Since
   \[ \partial_V\circ \varphi^{-n}(x)=\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_1)\varphi^{-n}(v_1)+\theta\circ\varphi^{-n}(x_2)\varphi^{-n}(v_2)\]
    and the image of $\exp^*_{K_n}$ lies in $K_n\otimes{\mathrm{Fil}}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$, it follows that 
   \[ \exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n}(x)=
    \begin{cases}
    (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\varphi^{-2m}(x_1)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m\ge N$}, \\
    (-1)^mp^{-m}\theta\circ\varphi^{-(2m+1)}(x_2)v_1 & \text{ if $n=2m+1\ge N$}.
    \end{cases}
   \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute exp* o h^1 in terms of theta o phi^{-n}(x_i).

nodes.name: PP14 step 3
nodes.statement:
Extend the trace map $\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}$ to the map $\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\mathrm{id}$ on $K_n\otimes_{\mathbb Q_p}\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)$. Then, $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^1$ if and only if
   \[
   \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/K_{n-1}}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n}(x)=p^{-1}\exp^*_{K_{n-2}}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},{n-2}}(x)
   \]
   for all even $n\ge N+2$.
nodes.statement_short: Reformulate membership via traces of exp*.

nodes.name: PP14 step 4
nodes.statement:
But 
   \[
   \mathrm{Tr}_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}}\circ \exp^*_{K_{m}} =\exp^*_{K_{m-1}}\circ {\mathrm{cor}}_{K_m\slash K_{m-1}}
   \]
   for all $m\ge0$, so we deduce that $x\in H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^1$ if and only if
   \[
   \exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n-1}(x)=p^{-1}\mathrm{Tr}_{K_{n-1}/K_{n-2}}\circ\exp^*_{K_{n-1}}\circ h^1_{\mathrm{Iw},n-1}(x)
   \]
   for all even $n\ge N-2$.

nodes.name: H^1_Iw(K,T)^i as inverse limit of finite-level conditions
nodes.statement:
For $i\in\{1,2\}$ and $n\geq N+1$, define
   \[ H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}=\left\{x\in H^1(K_n,T):\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n\slash K_m}\circ\exp^*_{K_n}(x)\in K_{m-1}\cdot v_1\hspace{2ex}\text{for all $m\in S_{N,i}^n$}\right\}.\]
   where $S_{N,i}^n$ is given by
   \begin{eqnarray*}
    S_{N,1}^n&=&\left\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ odd }\right\},\\
    S_{N,2}^n&=&\left\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ even }\right\}.
   \end{eqnarray*}
   Then $H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(K,T)^i=\varprojlim H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Defines finite-level conditions H^1_N(K_n,T)^{(i)} via traces of exp* and shows their inverse limit is H^1_Iw(K,T)^i.

nodes.statement:
Let $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$ be the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Tate pairing. Then 
   \[
     H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T) = H^1(K_n,T)\cap \exp_{K_n}\left( \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)} \otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V) \right)
   \]

nodes.name: Proof of PP17
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{3des}, we have
   \begin{equation} H^1_{f,N,(1)}(K_n,T)=\left(\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\cdot v_1\right)\right)^{\bot_{[,]}}
   \end{equation}
where $(\star)^{\bot_{[,]}}$ denotes the exact annihilator of $\star$ under the pairing $[\sim,\sim]$. But
\[
[\exp_{K_n}(\sim),\sim]=\mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/\mathbb Q_p}\langle\sim,\exp^*_{K_n}(\sim)\rangle.
\] 
where $\langle\sim,\sim\rangle$ is the pairing
\[
\langle\sim,\sim\rangle:\Big(K_n\otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\Big)\times\Big(K_n\otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\Big)\rightarrow K_n.
\] 
Therefore,
\begin{equation} x\in\left(\left(\exp^*_{K_n}\right)^{-1}\left(\star\cdot v_1\right)\right)^{\bot_{[,]}}\quad\text{if and only if}\quad x\in\exp_{K_n}\left((\star)^\bot\otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\right)
\end{equation}
     where $(\star)^\bot$ denotes the orthogonal complement of $\star$ under the pairing
     \begin{align*}
      K_n\times K_n &\rightarrow \mathbb Q_p\\
      (x,y) &\mapsto \mathrm{Tr}_{K_n/\mathbb Q_p}(xy).
     \end{align*}
    By linear algebra, we have
\[
\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\right)^\bot=\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}.
\]
Hence the result on combining \eqref{E} with \eqref{ortho}.
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 4.9 and the duality between exp and exp* under the Tate pairing, then linear algebra of trace-zero pieces.

nodes.name: Bloch-Kato exponential isomorphism
nodes.statement:
Recall that the exponential map $\exp_{K_n}$ gives an isomorphism
\[
\exp_{K_n}:K_n\otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)/\mathrm{Fil}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\rTo H^1_f(K_n,V).
\]

nodes.statement: We write $\exp_{K_n}^{-1}$ for its inverse.

nodes.name: Projection P^n_{N,i}
nodes.statement:
By \eqref{pro}, we may define a projection map
\[
P_{N,i}^n:K_n\rTo K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_m^{(0)}.
\]

nodes.name: H^1_{f,N,(i)} via the projection P
nodes.statement:
For $i=1,2$, we have
\[
 H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T) = \left\{x\in H_{f}^1(K_n,T):\left(P_{N,i}^n\otimes{\rm id}\right)\circ\exp_{K_n}^{-1}(x)=0\right\}.
\]

nodes.name: Proof of PP18
nodes.statement:
Note that
\[
K_n=\left(K_N\oplus\bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i'}^n}K_m^{(0)}\right)\oplus\left( \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\right).
\]
Therefore, 
\[
\left(P_{N,i}^n\otimes{\rm id}\right)\circ\exp_{K_n}^{-1}(x)=0\quad\text{if and only if}\quad\exp_{K_n}^{-1}(x)\in \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)/\mathrm{Fil}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V).
\]
nodes.statement_short: Split K_n into the two complementary sums and read off the kernel of the projection.

nodes.name: Formal group logarithm/exponential diagram
nodes.statement:
Recall that we have a commutative diagram
  






  
  \begin{diagram}
   {\rm tan}(\hat{E}\slash K_n) & \lTo^{\supset \hspace{3ex}} & \log_{\hat{E}}(\mathcal{O}_{K_n}) & \lTo^{\log_{\hat{E}}}& \hat{E}(\mathcal{O}_{K_n}) & \rTo^{\subset} & \hat{E}(\mathcal{O}_{K_n})\otimes \mathbb Q_p \\
   \dTo^{\cong}_i           & & & & &               & \dTo^{\delta} \\
   K_n\otimes \mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)\slash \mathrm{Fil}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V) & & & \rTo^{\exp_{K_n}} & & & H^1(K_n,V)
  \end{diagram}
  where $\delta$ is the Kummer map.

nodes.name: Jumping conditions on the formal group
nodes.statement_short: The image of H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T) in E-hat(O_{K_n}) is the group E-hat^i_N cut out by Kobayashi-type trace (jumping) conditions.
also_stated_at:
We define for a large integer $N$, which depends on $F$,
  \[
   \hat{E}_N^i(\mathcal{O}_{F_n})   := \left\{x\in\hat{E}(\mathcal{O}_{F_n}): \mathrm{Tr}_{F_n/F_m}x\in \hat{E}(\mathcal{O}_{F_{m-1}}))\text{ for all }m\in S_{N,i'}^n \text{ and }\mathrm{Tr}_{F_n/F_N}x=0\right\},
  \]
  where
  \begin{align*}
   S_{N,1'}^n&=\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ even}\};\\
   S_{N,2'}^n&=\{m\in[N+1,n]:m\text{ odd}\}.
  \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of PP19
nodes.statement:
By the comutative diagram above and Proposition~\ref{describingortho}, we have 
    \[
     \delta(x)\in H_{f,N,(i)}^1(K_n,T)\quad\text{if and only if}\quad i\circ\log_{\hat{E}}(x)\in \bigoplus_{m\in S_{N,i}^n}K_{m}^{(0)}\otimes\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V)/\mathrm{Fil}^0\mathbb D_{\mathrm{cris}}(V).
    \] 
    Since $\log_{\hat{E}}$ is injective (by Assumption~\ref{assumptionptorsion}) and compatible with the trace maps, we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Commutative diagram plus Proposition 4.12; injectivity of log by Assumption 4.10.

nodes.name: Selmer groups with jumping conditions Sel^{(i)}_N
nodes.statement:
Let $L$ be a number field and $N$ is an integer such that $N\ge N(L_w,V)$ for all primes $w$of $L$ above $p$. For $i=1,2$, we define the Selmer groups
   \[
   \mathrm{Sel}^{(i)}_N(E/L_n)=\ker\left(\mathrm{Sel}(E/L_n)\rTo \bigoplus_{w\mid p}\frac{H^1(L_{n,w},E_{p^\infty})}{\hat{E}_N^i(\mathcal{O}_{L_{n,w}})\otimes\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p }\right)
   \]
   for $n\ge N+1$. Moreover, we define
   \[
    \mathrm{Sel}^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)=\varinjlim_{n\ge N+1}\mathrm{Sel}^{(i)}_N(E/L_n)=\ker\left(\mathrm{Sel}(E/L_\infty)\rTo \bigoplus_{\omega\mid p} \frac{H^1(L_{\infty,\omega},E_{p^\infty})}{\hat{E}_N^i(\mathcal{O}_{L_{\infty,\omega}})\otimes\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p} \right)
   \]
   where $\hat{E}_N^i(\mathcal{O}_{L_{\infty,\omega}})=\varinjlim \hat{E}_N^i(\mathcal{O}_{L_{n,\omega\cap L_n}})$.

nodes.name: Annihilator of H^1_N is H^1_{f,N} tensor Q_p/Z_p
nodes.statement:
Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $n\ge N(K,V)$. For $i=1,2$, the exact annihilator of $H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)}$ under the Pontryagin duality
   \[
    [\sim,\sim]: H^1(K_n,T)\times H^1(K_n,E_{p^\infty})\rTo\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p
   \]
   is isomorphic to $H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)\otimes\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p$ for $i=1,2$.
assumptions: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $n\ge N(K,V)$

nodes.name: Proof of PP20
nodes.statement:
This essentially follows from \cite[proofs of Lemma~8.17 and Proposition~8.18]{kobayashi03}. By definition, we have an exact sequence
   \[
    0\rTo H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i)} \rTo H^1(K_n,T)\rTo\mathrm{Hom}\left(H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T),\mathbb Z_p\right).
   \]
   On taking Pontryagin duals, we obtain a second exact sequence
   \[
    H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)\otimes\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p\rTo H^1(K_n,E_{p^\infty})\rTo H_N^1(K_n,T)^{(i),\vee}\rTo0.
   \]
   Therefore, it remains to show that the first map above is injective. But $[px,y]=p[x,y]$ for all $x,y\in H^1(K_n,T)$. This implies that if $x\in H^1(K_n,T)$ such that $px\in H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$, then $x\in H^1_{f,N,(i)}(K_n,T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Following Kobayashi: dualise an exact sequence and show the first map is injective by p-divisibility.

nodes.name: The two definitions of signed Selmer groups coincide
nodes.statement:
The two definitions of signed Selmer groups coincide, namely, 
   \[
   \mathrm{Sel}^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)=\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/L_\infty)
   \]
   for $i=1,2$.
conclusions:
\label{samesel}
   The two definitions of signed Selmer groups coincide, namely, 
   \[
   \mathrm{Sel}^{(i)}_N(E/L_\infty)=\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/L_\infty)
   \]
   for $i=1,2$.

We show that if we define $\mathrm{Sel}_N^{(i)}(E/K_n)$ by replacing the local conditions at places above $p$ in the definition of $\mathrm{Sel}(E/K_n)$ by these ``jumping conditions", then  for $i=1,2$ we have isomorphisms

nodes.name: Proof of PP22
nodes.statement:
It suffices to show that for any finite extensions $K$ of $\mathbb Q_p$, we have

nodes.name: p-adic Lie extension L_infty and G
nodes.statement: Let $L_\infty$ be a $p$-adic Lie extension of $\mathbb Q$ containing $\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^\infty})$, so $G=\mathrm{Gal}(L_\infty\slash\mathbb Q)$ is a compact $p$-adic Lie group of finite rank.

nodes.statement: Let $H=\mathrm{Gal}(L_\infty\slash \mathbb Q(\mu_{p^\infty}))$.

nodes.name: Approximating fields L_m
nodes.statement: Choose a sequence of finite extensions $L_m$ of $\mathbb Q$ such that $L_\infty=\varinjlim L_m$ and $L^{(m)}_\infty=L_m(\mu_{p^\infty})$ is Galois over $\mathbb Q$ for all $m\geq 0$.

nodes.name: Signed Selmer groups over p-adic Lie extensions and duals X_i
nodes.statement:
For $i=1,2$, we define $\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/L_\infty):=\varinjlim_m\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/L^{(m)}_\infty)$ for $=1,2$ and write
   \[ X_i(E\slash L_\infty)=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{cts}}\left(\mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_\infty),\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p\right). \]

nodes.name: Category M_H(G)
nodes.statement: Denote by $\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$ the category of finitely generated $\Lambda(G)$-modules $M$ for which $M\slash M(p)$ is finitely generated over $\Lambda(H)$. Here $M(p)$ denotes the $p$-torsion part of $M$.

nodes.name: M_H(G)-conjecture
nodes.statement: The ${\mathfrak M}_H(G)$-conjecture in \cite{cfksv} states that the Pontryagin dual of the Selmer group of $E$ over $L_\infty$ is an element of ${\mathfrak M}_H(G)$ if $E$ has good ordinary reduction at $p$.
conclusions: the Pontryagin dual of the Selmer group of $E$ over $L_\infty$ is an element of ${\mathfrak M}_H(G)$

nodes.statement: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$. Define the Galois groups $G=\mathrm{Gal}(L_\infty\slash\mathbb Q)$ and $H=\mathrm{Gal}(L_\infty\slash \mathbb Q(\mu_p))$. Then $X_i(E\slash L_\infty)\in\mathfrak{M}_H(G)$ for $i=1,2$.
assumptions: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$.

nodes.name: Control of signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement:
Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$. Let $L_\infty$ be a $p$-adic Lie extension of $\mathbb Q$ containing $\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^\infty})$, and let $H=\mathrm{Gal}(L_\infty\slash \mathbb Q(\mu_{p^\infty}))$. Assume also that $E(L_{v,\infty})$ has no $p$-torsion for any prime $v$ of $L$ above $p$.  Then for $i=1,2$, the kernel and cokernel of the restriction map 
   \[
   \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash \mathbb Q_\infty)\rTo \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_\infty)^H
   \]
   are cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-modules.
assumptions: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over $\mathbb Q$ with good supersingular reduction at $p$ and $a_p=0$.
Assume also that $E(L_{v,\infty})$ has no $p$-torsion for any prime $v$ of $L$ above $p$.
conclusions:
Then for $i=1,2$, the kernel and cokernel of the restriction map 
   \[

nodes.name: Conjecture 6.1 and mu=0 give finite generation over Lambda(H)
nodes.statement: Assume $H$ is pro-$p$, and that Conjecture~\ref{support} holds. If $\mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash\mathbb Q_\infty)$ is a cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module, which is equivalent to the vanishing of the $\mu$-invariant of $X_i(E/\slash\mathbb Q_\infty)$ as conjectured in \cite[\S10]{kobayashi03}, then we can apply Nakayama's lemma (c.f. for example \cite[Theorem 2.6]{coateshowson01}) to deduce that $X_i(E\slash L_\infty)$ is finitely generated over $\Lambda(H)$.
nodes.statement_short: If H is pro-p, Conjecture 6.1 holds and mu=0 for the cyclotomic signed Selmer groups, Nakayama gives X_i(E/L_infty) f.g. over Lambda(H).

nodes.name: Finite places S_f and I_v^i
nodes.statement: Write $S_f$ for the set of finite places of $S$ and let $I_v^i$ be as defined in Section~\ref{supersingular}.

nodes.name: Poitou-Tate exact sequences for signed Selmer groups
nodes.statement:
By \cite[\S A.3]{perrinriou95}, there are two exact sequences
  \begin{align}
   &0\rightarrow\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo H^1(G_S(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n})),E_{p^\infty})\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f}J_v^i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo H^1_i(\mathbb Q,T)^\vee\rTo\cdots \\
   &0\rightarrow H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)\rTo^{f_n}H^1(G_S(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n})),E_{p^\infty})\rTo^{g_n}\bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo\cdots \end{align}
  where $H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)$ is defined by
  \[
   \ker\Big(H^1(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)\rTo\prod_{v\in S_f}I^i_v(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\Big)
  \]
  and $M^\vee$ denotes the Pontryagin dual of $M$.

nodes.name: Poitou-Tate sequences
nodes.statement:
&0\rightarrow\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo H^1(G_S(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n})),E_{p^\infty})\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f}J_v^i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo H^1_i(\mathbb Q,T)^\vee\rTo\cdots \\
   &0\rightarrow H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)\rTo^{f_n}H^1(G_S(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n})),E_{p^\infty})\rTo^{g_n}\bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\rTo\cdots
nodes.label: firstpt

nodes.name: Surjectivity onto finite local quotients
nodes.statement:
The natural map
   \[
   H^1\big(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty),E_{p^\infty}\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)
   \]
   is surjective.
conclusions:
The natural map
   \[
   H^1\big(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty),E_{p^\infty}\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)
   \]
   is surjective.

nodes.name: Proof of PP23
nodes.statement:
On taking inverse limit, we have
   \[
    \varprojlim_n\Big( \bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\Big) = \frac{H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)}{H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)^i}
   \]
   and $\displaystyle\varprojlim_n g_n$ is injective by \cite[Theorem~7.3]{kobayashi03}. Therefore, on taking inverse limit in \eqref{secondpt}, we have 
   \[\varprojlim_n H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)=0,\]
   which implies that $\displaystyle\varinjlim_n H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)^\vee=0$. Therefore, on taking direct limit in \eqref{firstpt}, we have an exact sequence
   \[
    0\rTo\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q_\infty)\rTo H^1\big(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty),E_{p^\infty}\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)\rTo 0
   \]
   and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Inverse limit of the second Poitou-Tate sequence vanishes by Kobayashi; dualise and pass to direct limit in the first.

nodes.name: PP23 step 1
nodes.statement:
On taking inverse limit, we have
   \[
    \varprojlim_n\Big( \bigoplus_{v\in S_f}I_v^i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}))\Big) = \frac{H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)}{H^1_{\mathrm{Iw}}(\mathbb Q_p,T)^i}
   \]
   and $\displaystyle\varprojlim_n g_n$ is injective by \cite[Theorem~7.3]{kobayashi03}.
nodes.statement_short: Inverse limit of local terms; injectivity of lim g_n by Kobayashi.

nodes.name: PP23 step 2
nodes.statement:
Therefore, on taking inverse limit in \eqref{secondpt}, we have 
   \[\varprojlim_n H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)=0,\]
   which implies that $\displaystyle\varinjlim_n H^1_i(\mathbb Q(\mu_{p^n}),T)^\vee=0$.
nodes.statement_short: Inverse limit of H^1_i vanishes, so its dual direct limit vanishes.

nodes.name: PP23 step 3
nodes.statement:
Therefore, on taking direct limit in \eqref{firstpt}, we have an exact sequence
   \[
    0\rTo\mathrm{Sel}^i(E/\mathbb Q_\infty)\rTo H^1\big(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty),E_{p^\infty}\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S_f} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)\rTo 0
   \]
   and we are done.
nodes.statement_short: Direct limit of (14) gives the surjectivity.

nodes.name: Surjectivity of the global-to-local map
nodes.statement:
The natural map
   \[
   H^1\big(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty),E_{p^\infty}\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)
   \]
   is surjective.
conclusions:
\label{surjectivity}
   The natural map
   \[
   H^1\big(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty),E_{p^\infty}\big)\rTo\bigoplus_{v\in S} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)
   \]
   is surjective.
nodes.label: surjectivity

nodes.name: Proof of PP24
nodes.statement: This follows as $J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty)=0$ for $p\neq2$ if $v$ is an infinite prime.
nodes.statement_short: Infinite place contributes nothing for p odd.

nodes.name: Fundamental diagram
nodes.statement:
We attempted to prove Conjecture~\ref{support} by studying the following commutative diagram, which we call {\it the fundamental diagram}.
   
   \begin{diagram}
    0 & \rTo & \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash L_\infty)^{H} & \rTo & H^1(G_S(L_\infty),E_{p^\infty})^{H} & \rTo & \bigoplus_{v\in S}J_v^i(L_\infty)^{H} & &\\   
      &      & \uTo^{\alpha}      &      &   \uTo^{\beta}              &      & \uTo^{\gamma=(\gamma_v)} & & \\
    0 & \rTo & \mathrm{Sel}^i(E\slash \mathbb Q_\infty) & \rTo & H^1(G_S(\mathbb Q_\infty,E_{p^\infty}) & \rTo & \bigoplus_{v\in S} J_v^i(\mathbb Q_\infty) & \rTo & 0    
   \end{diagram}
   where the $J_v^i$ are as defined in Section~\ref{supersingular}.

nodes.name: Snake lemma sequence
nodes.statement:
Applying the snake lemma gives a long exact sequence
  \[ 0 \rTo \ker(\alpha) \rTo \ker(\beta) \rTo \ker(\gamma) \rTo \mathrm{coker}(\alpha)\rTo \mathrm{coker}(\beta).\]

nodes.name: Reduction of Conjecture 6.1 to beta and gamma
nodes.statement: In order to prove Conjecture~\ref{support}, it is therefore sufficient to show that the kernel and cokernel of the map $\beta$ and the kernel of $\gamma$ are cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-modules.

nodes.name: beta and gamma_v for v not over p
nodes.statement: The results for $\beta$ and for $\gamma_v$, $v\nmid p$, are easy consequences of the inflation-restriction exact sequences (c.f. \cite{coatessujatha00}).

nodes.name: Reduction of Conjecture 6.1 to Conjecture 6.4
nodes.statement:
The main difficulty is the study of the kernel of the local restriction map $\gamma_v$ when $v\mid p$. Let $K$ be the completion of $L$ at such a prime, and write $\mathcal{H}$ for the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(K_\infty\slash \mathbb Q_{p,\infty})$. In order to prove Conjecture~\ref{support}, we may use the local conditions from Section~\ref{alter} and attempt to show that the kernel of the map
  \[
   \frac{H^1(\mathbb Q_{p,\infty},E_{p^\infty})}{\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p}\rTo\left(\frac{H^1(K_\infty,E_{p^\infty})}{\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p}\right)^\mathcal{H}
  \]
  is a cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module. Consider the following commutative diagram: 
  \begin{diagram}
   0&\rTo& \hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p&\rTo& H^1(\mathbb Q_{p,\infty},E_{p^\infty})&\rTo&  \frac{H^1(\mathbb Q_{p,\infty},E_{p^\infty})}{\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p}&\rTo& 0\\
    &      & \dTo             &      & \dTo              &      &   \dTo                   & & \\  
   0&\rTo& \left( \hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p\right)^\mathcal{H}&\rTo&\left( H^1(K_{\infty},E_{p^\infty})\right)^\mathcal{H}&\rTo&  \left(\frac{H^1(K_{\infty},E_{p^\infty})}{\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p}\right)^\mathcal{H}&& 
  \end{diagram}
  where the vertical maps are restrictions. The the first two maps are injective by Assumption~\ref{assumptionptorsion}. By the snake lemma, the kernel of the third map is bounded by the cokernel of the first, so it is sufficient to show that the cokernel of the restriction map
  \[ \hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb Q_{p,\infty}})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p\rTo \left( \hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\otimes\mathbb Q_p\slash\mathbb Z_p\right)^\mathcal{H}\]
  is a cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module. By taking $\mathcal{H}$-cohomology of the short exact sequence
  \[
   0\rTo \hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\rTo\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\otimes \mathbb Q_p\rTo\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\otimes\mathbb Q_p/\mathbb Z_p\rTo0,
  \]
  we may reduce the validity of Conjecture~\ref{support} to the following conjecture.
nodes.statement_short: Via a local diagram, the snake lemma and H-cohomology, Conjecture 6.1 reduces to cofinite generation of H^1(H, E-hat^i_N).

nodes.name: Cofinite generation of H^1(H, E-hat^i_N)
nodes.statement: The cohomological group $H^1\left(\mathcal{H},\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\right)$ is a cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module.
conclusions:
\label{cofcoh}
   The cohomological group $H^1\left(\mathcal{H},\hat{E}^i_N(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\right)$ is a cofinitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module.
nodes.label: cofcoh

nodes.name: Coates-Greenberg vanishing
nodes.statement: Note that it is shown in \cite[Theorem~3.1]{coatesgreenberg} that $H^1\left(\mathcal{H},\hat{E}(\mathcal{O}_{K_\infty})\right)=0$.
